# defineTheme

Builds a theme: the full token set (your overrides over the Ouro defaults) and the CSS custom properties that apply it. Put `css` in a stylesheet loaded after `@ouro.bot/ui/styles.css`.

```tsx
import { defineTheme } from "@ouro.bot/ui/theme";
```

## Example

```tsx
const { css } = defineTheme({ color: { accent: { light: "#c2410c", dark: "#fb923c" } } });
const { css: brand } = defineTheme({ radius: { control: "999px" } }, { selector: ".brand" });
```

## Usage

Use `opts.selector` to scope a theme to a subtree instead of `:root`. `on-<tone>` defaults to white (light) or black (dark). `soft-<tone>` and `<tone>-ink` are only emitted when you set them; otherwise the utilities derive them with `color-mix` over the base variables where they are used, so a scoped override of a base color reaches them. Text on a soft background uses `<tone>-ink`, not the plain tone.

Colors are emitted as `light-dark(light, dark)`. Switching the scheme on the root (`data-theme` on `<html>`, or the OS setting) always works. A scheme set on a wrapper (`color-scheme: dark` on a subtree) needs native `light-dark()` support: if your CSS pipeline lowers it for older browsers (Lightning CSS, Tailwind's optimizer), the lowered tokens resolve once at the root and the wrapper's scheme is ignored.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `partial` | `DeepPartial<ThemeTokens>` | `{}` |
| `opts` | `{ selector?: string }` | `{}` |

## Returns

`DefinedTheme`

## Types

### `BaseColorName`

The colors every theme sets: page surfaces, text, lines and the five tones.

```ts
type BaseColorName = "surface" | "surface-raised" | "ink" | "ink-muted" | "line" | ToneName;
```

### `DeepPartial`

Every key optional, at every depth: the shape `defineTheme` takes for overrides.

```ts
type DeepPartial<T> = {
  [K in keyof T]?: (T[K] extends object ? DeepPartial<T[K]> : T[K]) | undefined;
};
```

### `DefinedTheme`

What `defineTheme` returns: the merged tokens and the CSS that applies them.

```ts
type DefinedTheme = { tokens: ThemeTokens; css: string };
```

### `DerivedColorName`

`on-<tone>` is the text color on a solid tone. `soft-<tone>` is the tone's tinted background, and text on it uses `<tone>-ink` (the tone darkened toward `ink`), never the plain tone, which fails 4.5:1 in light mode.

```ts
type DerivedColorName = `on-${ToneName}` | `soft-${ToneName}` | `${InkToneName}-ink`;
```

### `InkToneName`

Tones that have a `<tone>-ink` text color for use on `soft-<tone>`. Neutral uses `ink`.

```ts
type InkToneName = Exclude<ToneName, "neutral">;
```

### `SchemeColor`

A color that has one value per color scheme.

```ts
type SchemeColor = { light: string; dark: string };
```

### `ThemeTokens`

All token groups of a theme. `on-<tone>` and `soft-<tone>` are derived when not given.

```ts
type ThemeTokens = {
  color: Record<BaseColorName, SchemeColor> & Partial<Record<DerivedColorName, SchemeColor>>;
  radius: { control: string; surface: string; pill: string };
  font: { body: string; display: string; mono: string };
  motion: {
    /** Milliseconds. */
    fast: number;
    base: number;
    slow: number;
    spring: { visualDuration: number; bounce: number };
    /** Scale applied while a control is pressed. */
    pressScale: number;
  };
  z: { overlay: number; popover: number; toast: number };
  /** The dimming layer behind sheets and dialogs. */
  backdrop: {
    color: SchemeColor;
    /** Opacity when the sheet or dialog is fully open. A dragged sheet fades it toward 0. */
    opacity: number;
  };
};
```

### `ToneName`

The five tones every component maps its `tone` prop to.

```ts
type ToneName = "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger";
```
